title: Follow Ezra from Babylon to Jerusalem

babylon.name: Babylon
babylon.text: The great city on the Euphrates, by Ezra's time part of the Persian Empire. Ezra began his journey from Babylon (Ezra 7:6, 9). Its ruins lie near Hillah in Iraq, about 54 miles (86 km) south of Baghdad.
babylon.label: b

ahava.name: Ahava Canal
ahava.text: Ezra gathered the travelers at the canal that flows toward Ahava and camped there three days (Ezra 8:15). The place was somewhere in Babylonia, but its location has not been identified, so this marker is only approximate.
ahava.label: tl

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.text: Ezra arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month (Ezra 7:8–9). The temple had been completed in the sixth year of King Darius (Ezra 6:15), almost sixty years before the traditional date of Ezra's arrival.

baghdad.name: Baghdad
baghdad.text: Capital of modern Iraq, shown for orientation.

damascus.name: Damascus
damascus.text: Capital of modern Syria, shown for orientation. Caravans between Mesopotamia and Judah commonly passed through or near it.

chapters.title: A teacher of the Law in Babylon
chapters.html:
Ezra was a priest descended from Aaron and a teacher well versed in the Law of Moses. He had devoted himself to studying the Law, keeping it and teaching it.

In the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, the king gave him a letter authorizing him to lead any willing Israelites to Jerusalem, carry gifts for the temple and appoint judges who knew God's laws.
facts: The king's letter in Ezra 7:12–26 is written in Aramaic, the international language of the Persian Empire, while the surrounding story is in Hebrew.
The 458 BC date assumes the king was Artaxerxes I. Some scholars think Ezra came later, under Artaxerxes II.

chapters.title: Fasting by the canal
chapters.html:
Ezra assembled the families at the canal flowing toward Ahava. Finding no Levites among them, he sent for some from a place called Kasiphia, and they came.

Ezra was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers after telling him that God protects those who look to him. So he proclaimed a fast, and the people humbled themselves and asked God for a safe journey.
quote: The gracious hand of our God is on everyone who looks to him
facts: Ezra lists the family heads who came with him (Ezra 8:1–14). The men counted there total about 1,500, not including women and children.
Kasiphia, like Ahava, has never been located. It was apparently a community in Babylonia with a group of Levites and temple servants.

chapters.title: Four months on the road
chapters.html:
Ezra weighed out the silver, gold and temple articles and entrusted them to twelve leading priests to guard. The group set out from the Ahava Canal on the twelfth day of the first month.

They reached Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, and Ezra says God protected them from enemies and bandits along the way. The book does not describe the route, so the map marks only the endpoints.
facts: Babylon and Jerusalem are about 540 miles (870 km) apart in a straight line. Travelers usually avoided the desert between them and followed the Fertile Crescent, a much longer trip.
Ezra 7:9 dates the start of the journey to the first day of the first month, so the whole trip, including the stop at Ahava, took four months.

chapters.title: Grief in the rain
chapters.html:
After three days of rest, the treasure was weighed in the temple and the travelers offered sacrifices. Then leaders reported that many people, including priests and Levites, had married women from the surrounding peoples.

Ezra tore his clothes and prayed in grief. The people assembled in the square before the temple, trembling in the heavy rain, and agreed to deal with the matter.
facts: The assembly met on the twentieth day of the ninth month (Ezra 10:9), in early winter, the season of the heavy rains in Jerusalem.
Ezra 10:18–44 ends the book with a list of the men who had married foreign wives, including members of priestly families.

chapters.title: Reading the Law at the Water Gate
chapters.html:
In Nehemiah's time, the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate and asked Ezra to bring out the Book of the Law. He stood on a high wooden platform and read aloud from daybreak until noon.

Levites helped the people understand what was read. The people wept, but they were told to celebrate, and they kept the Festival of Tabernacles by living in shelters.
facts: Nehemiah 8:4 names thirteen men who stood beside Ezra on the platform, six on his right and seven on his left.
Scholars debate the order of Ezra's and Nehemiah's missions. Nehemiah 8 is the main passage that shows the two men together.
